content.value_statement: Single-cell analyses require careful model and workflow choices across diverse modalities. This skill provides scvi-tools guidance for preprocessing, model selection, training, integration, and interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Recommends scvi-tools models for RNA, ATAC, multimodal, spatial, methylation, cytometry, and velocity data.
Explains AnnData preparation, raw-count handling, feature selection, and technical covariate registration.
Outlines model training, latent representation extraction, normalized expression, downstream clustering, and model persistence.
Guides Bayesian differential expression, effect thresholds, batch handling, output interpretation, and special comparisons.
Covers batch integration, reference mapping, hyperparameter tuning, GPU use, and memory-efficient workflows.
Compares models for CITE-seq, multiome, spatial deconvolution, cell annotation, and specialized modalities.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but includes no executable scripts, trained models, or datasets.
Users must install compatible scvi-tools, Scanpy, PyTorch, and related dependencies.
Recommended parameters require validation against dataset size, modality, experimental design, and software version.
Results still require biological review and appropriate statistical validation.

use_cases.title: Integrate scRNA-seq Studies
use_cases.description: Build a raw-count workflow for batch correction, latent embedding, clustering, and differential expression across studies.

use_cases.title: Select a Multi-omics Model
use_cases.description: Compare totalVI, MultiVI, and related models for paired or unpaired RNA, protein, and accessibility measurements.

use_cases.title: Optimize Large Analyses
use_cases.description: Plan GPU training, memory management, hyperparameter tuning, persistence, and troubleshooting for large single-cell datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [modality] data in AnnData with [batch details]. Recommend an scvi-tools model and outline preprocessing, setup fields, and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Complete Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scvi-tools workflow for [dataset description]. Include quality control, raw-count preservation, AnnData registration, training, latent extraction, and model saving.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a dataset description into an analysis plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design Differential Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Design differential expression analysis comparing [group 1] and [group 2] by [group key]. Explain mode, delta, batch handling, and result interpretation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare biological groups with a trained model.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Advanced Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an advanced integration of [modalities] across [studies or batches]. Compare suitable models, covariates, validation checks, memory strategy, and reproducibility steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate a complex multi-study or multi-omics project.

output_examples.input: Recommend a model for batch-corrected scRNA-seq annotation with few labeled cells.
output: Use scANVI for semi-supervised annotation after preparing a suitable scVI representation.
Register raw counts, batch labels, known cell labels, and the unlabeled category.
Validate transferred labels by batch, donor, confidence, and known marker expression.

output_examples.input: Plan spatial deconvolution using a labeled single-cell reference.
output: Use DestVI when cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific expression are required.
Train the reference model first, then align genes and labels with spatial data.
Inspect proportions, spatial patterns, reference coverage, and model stability before interpretation.

output_examples.input: Explain a differential expression comparison between treatment groups.
output: Define the grouping field, comparison groups, effect-size threshold, and batch strategy.
Use change mode when a meaningful minimum effect is required.
Interpret posterior evidence, effect size, expression estimates, and false-discovery control together.

best_practices: Preserve raw counts before normalization and register the correct AnnData layer.
Register known technical covariates, then validate biological structure and batch mixing.
Save trained models, analysis-ready AnnData objects, parameters, versions, and random seeds.
anti_patterns: Do not train count models on log-normalized values when raw counts are required.
Do not accept batch-corrected embeddings without checking biological conservation and technical mixing.
Do not choose models without matching their modality, pairing assumptions, and required data fields.

faq.question: Which data modalities are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance covers RNA, ATAC, CITE-seq, multiome, spatial, methylation, cytometry, velocity, and related single-cell data.

faq.question: Does this skill run analyses automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides model guidance, workflow structure, examples, interpretation help, and troubleshooting information.

faq.question: Why are raw counts important?
faq.answer: Many scvi-tools models use count likelihoods and expect unnormalized values in the registered AnnData matrix or layer.

faq.question: Is a GPU required?
faq.answer: No. A GPU can reduce training time for large datasets, while smaller analyses can run on a CPU.

faq.question: How should batch correction be validated?
faq.answer: Check technical mixing, biological conservation, known markers, donor effects, cluster stability, and downstream conclusions.

faq.question: Will every example match my installed version?
faq.answer: Not always. Verify model availability, parameters, and APIs against the official documentation for your installed scvi-tools version.
